items.headline: Can We Defend Against AI-Generated Video Attacks on Real-World Crisis Events? A Systematic Evaluation of Detectors, Generators and Social Dissemination
items.dek: Recent video generators can fabricate realistic depictions of wars, disasters, public emergencies, and other real-world crises, creating substantial risks of misinformation.
items.author: Shuo Liang, Yixing Ma, Pengfei Zhou, ... Kaipeng Zhang, Wangbo Zhao (38 authors)
items.caption: arXiv abstract page (v2, revised 2026-08-17): title, authors, abstract
items.notes: Submitted 14 Aug 2026 (v1), revised 17 Aug 2026 (v2). 63 pages, 20 figures, 32 tables. License: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license (not CC). Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/liangshuo0111/RA-Bench (public, not gated; no README/LICENSE file in the repo).

items.slide_topic: Which one is real? (video Turing test quiz)
items.dek: Figure 1 | Which is which? Real and AI-generated clips from four crisis scenarios are paired side by side; identify the synthetic example in each pair before consulting the answer key on the following page.
items.caption: Paper's own 'CAN YOU TELL — REAL OR GENERATED?' teaser: 4 scenarios (I Military alert, II Fuel-tank fire, III Wildfire recon, IV Pandemic lockdown/vaccination), 2 columns x 5 frames each
items.notes: 1867x1182 PNG from arxiv.org/html/2608.14391v2/fengmian_v6.png. Answer key, verbatim from PDF p.2: 'Figure 1 answer key (from page 1; left/right): I Generated/Real; II Real/Generated; III Real/Generated; IV Generated/Real.' The GIF pairs below are the actual clips for scenarios I, III and IV (matched by frame comparison; the AI clips are Seedance 2.0). Scenario II (Pasadena chemical-plant fire) uses AP footage that RA-Bench does not redistribute.

datasets.title: How 20 human reviewers labelled RA-Bench videos, by source (Stage 1, share of judgments)
datasets.source: RA-Bench, arXiv 2608.14391, Table 7 ('Human recognition varies sharply by generation source'). Open-source avg: 26.3/5.0/68.6; closed-source avg: 40.6/6.5/52.9; generated total (pooled): 33.9/5.8/60.3.

datasets.title: Human accuracy at spotting real vs AI videos: DF26 vs two older deepfake datasets
datasets.source: DF26, arXiv 2609.07369, Table 7 (232 labeling sessions; 30 videos each, 15 fake)

facts.claim: Reviewers identify 68.6% of open-source videos as generated, but only 52.9% of closed-source videos, with Seedance2.0 and Kling falling to 40.7% and 45.1%.
Seedance 2.0 fakes were judged 'Real' in 51.9% of reviewer judgments - versus 71.9% for genuine footage.
We use 633 generated videos that are labeled Real by all five reviewers to form RA-Bench-HumanProof.
facts.source: RA-Bench (verbatim); 160 of them from Kling and 159 from Seedance2.0

facts.claim: Real crisis footage was labelled 'Generated' in 22.8% of judgments: 'Real videos depicting crisis events can therefore also be mistaken for generated content.'
On RA-Bench-HumanProof, Gemini Binary and Diagnostic reach only 54.7% and 54.5% BAcc, while the seven traditional detectors average 47.5% AUC.
After a simulated social-media re-share (H.264 re-encode + half resolution + 8 fps + a synthetic news badge), fine-tuned AI-video detectors' mean fake-detection rate fell from 46.0% to 1.4%.
facts.source: RA-Bench Sec. 1 findings + Sec. 4.3.3 ('the Full condition of the social dissemination simulation reduces mean FakeR across the five fine-tuned configurations from 46.0% to 1.4%'; Full = T1 VP9-to-H.264 transcode + T2 0.5x downsampling + T3 8 fps + T4 synthetic news badge)

facts.claim: RA-Bench: 17,886 videos - 1,830 real crisis clips across 10 social-risk categories plus 16,056 AI clips from four open-source and five closed-source generators; 20 reviewers made 53,550 Stage-1 judgments.
Figure 1 answer key (from page 1; left/right): I Generated/Real; II Real/Generated; III Real/Generated; IV Generated/Real.
Accuracy on deepfakes from DF26 is 52.6%, near chance, compared to 74.5% and 69.8% on the other two, while accuracy on real videos is similar.
facts.source: DF26, arXiv 2609.07369 (verbatim; other two = CelebDF++ and DeepSpeak v2)

facts.claim: DF26 video files are a controlled-access Hugging Face dataset (DF26/DF26); its license forbids publishing or redistributing any part, so DF26 clips cannot be shown in the deck.

not_found.outline_item: DF26 (arXiv 2609.07369) real + AI video clips for the 'Which one is real?' slides (Fig. 1 triplets: real / Veo 3.1 / Kling 3.0)
not_found.searched: arXiv abs + HTML (only external link is https://huggingface.co/datasets/DF26/DF26), HF API (datasets/spaces/models linked to arxiv:2609.07369), DuckDuckGo for a project page/GitHub: none. The HF dataset (271 real + 2,420 fake mp4, 1280x720 H.264) is gated ('Request access to DF26'): every file returns HTTP 401 without an approved account; access requires submitting name, institution, institutional email and intended use and agreeing to the DF26 license. LICENSE.md Sec. 5: 'Users may not redistribute, sublicense, sell, publish, mirror, upload, or otherwise transfer the dataset, in whole or in part, to any third party' (small excerpts only 'when expressly permitted by the maintainers'); Sec. 7: commercial-generator clips 'may not be redistributed'. Access was NOT requested on the user's behalf. Replaced by RA-Bench (public, same real-vs-I2V-fake design).

Real clips used are US-government public domain (DVIDS, per metadata/real_rights_release.csv and the DVIDS pages). Credit 'RA-Bench, Liang et al., arXiv 2608.14391' on the slide/notes.

notes: DF26 clips are gated + no-redistribution, so the quiz media come from RA-Bench (arXiv 2608.14391, public HF dataset). 4 real/AI pairs = 8 looping GIFs (960x540, 24 fps, identical size/fps/frame count/start within each pair; 48-90 MB each, ~530 MB total) + matching 1280x720 MP4s and first-frame posters. Strongest set: fig1-wildfire and fig1-vaccination (paper Figure 1 AND HumanProof: all five reviewers called the AI clip real) plus either hp-trench (HumanProof) or fig1-military (Figure 1, not HumanProof). All AI clips: ByteDance Seedance 2.0 image-to-video from the real clip's first frame. Real clips: US DoD/DVIDS public domain. Original downloads kept in realfake_src/.
